waves.title: Pizza line
waves.sub: Har item ko line par rakho

signs: Chooses 1/8 of a pizza to get more
Orders unit fractions by the bottom number

because.rule: shown only to a child the learner model holds this mix-up for, at this beat; any other child gets the script's own board

judge.by: a separate Claude judge (Opus), packet only, p412+l1366
judge.notes: There is one fraction per item on a single 0 to 1 line with 8 ticks (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/3, 1/6), all of them correct positions. A child who thinks 1/8 > 1/4 would place 1/8 to the right of 1/4 and miss, so the mix-up is shown. No title or sub names a position or the rule ('Pizza line', 'Har item ko line par rakho', 'Ab apni jagah chuno'). Not counted: 1/3 and 1/6 do not fall on the eighths ticks, so the child has to estimate them. The 'WAVE 1/3' counter looks like a fraction on a fractions screen and might confuse a child. Many feedback strings are English ('landed', 'Run complete', 'SAME SPOT'), which is within Hinglish. Both screens are legible with nothing cut off.

judge2.by: a second separate Claude judge (Opus), packet only
judge2.notes: The child places one unit fraction at a time (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/3, 1/6) on a single 0-1 line, so 1/8 lands nearest 0 and 1/2 in the middle. That puts the whole-number-bias belief (1/8 > 1/4) where it visibly fails, and no title or sub gives a position away. Not counted as faults: 1/3 and 1/6 do not fall on the 8 scaffold ticks (I cannot tell how strictly 'EXACT' is graded there), several strings are English inside Hinglish ('Run complete', 'Toughest', 'SAME SPOT', 'landed'), the coach line 'Fraction ko line par pakdo' is low-contrast but legible, and p360 was not supplied.
